subject: MAP: Security acceptance criteria & retention for FinRise
messages:
From: Aisha Benton <aisha@finrise.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Liao <victor.liao@finrise.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — security gates + data retention needs

Evelyn,

Thanks for the chat this morning. As discussed, the FinRise procurement team needs a concrete MAP with explicit security/compliance acceptance gates before we unlock procurement and legal can sign the DPA. High-level asks from our side: 

- Clear SOC 2 scope (type II, controls mapping) and an expected delivery window for attestation evidence.
- SIG/CAIQ answers or a pointer to where we can view them.
- Draft DPA with specific retention windows and data residency options (US-only vs global).
- A1: Confirmation of log retention & access logs (how long, export format).
- A2: Backup & restore scope and any third-party subprocessors that touch data.

Can you send a MAP-style timeline (milestones & owners) and any artifacts you can share right away? Ideally we want an acceptance decision by the end of next week (3/28) — is that feasible?

Thanks,
Aisha Benton
Head of Vendor Risk | FinRise
attachments: none

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Benton <aisha@finrise.com>
Cc: Victor Liao <victor.liao@finrise.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — security gates + data retention needs

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. We put together a concise MAP and included the artifacts you asked for. Please find the draft attached (redwood_mpa_v1.2.pdf) and the DPA draft (DPA-FinRise-draft.docx). Summary of the proposal below: 

- SOC 2: Redwood will provide our latest Type II report (attestation letter attached) and a controls matrix mapping to the acceptance checklist. Expected formal attestation delivery: Q2 2027 (target: 2027-05-15). 
- SIG/CAIQ: Completed CAIQ with redwood responses is included in the attached MPA PDF and linked to our docs folder. 
- DPA: We attach a draft showing two retention tiers: standard (90 days transient cache; 180 days logs) and enterprise (configurable up to 7 yrs for logs/backups). We note region options: Hosted (multi-region) or US-only private deployment.
- Evidence/format: SOC2 attestation (PDF), CAIQ (spreadsheet & PDF), log export (JSONL), and audit logs (CSV).

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) 2027-03-21: MAP shared (this email) — owner: Redwood (Evelyn)
2) 2027-03-23: FinRise security review & Qs — owner: FinRise (Aisha)
3) 2027-03-25: Follow-up on any DPA redlines & retention choice — joint owners
4) 2027-03-28: FinRise acceptance decision (conditional) — owner: FinRise
5) 2027-04-05: Execute DPA & enable staging access for evidence capture — owner: Redwood

I think we can hit 3/28 for a conditional acceptance if there are no major open items. If FinRise needs the SOC 2 attestation earlier than 5/15 we can discuss a limited scope bridge (SOC2 letter + control snapshots) to satisfy gate A while we finalize the full attestation.

Would you prefer we call the MAP milestones out in a shared Google Sheet (I can create and share link)?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Compliance & Trust | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_mpa_v1.2.pdf; SOC2-letter-redwood-2026.pdf; DPA-FinRise-draft.docx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff — security gates + data retention needs

Irene / Connor — looping you both in. Aisha's team asked for the SOC2 evidence timeline and clarity on retention tiers. Quick notes / asks before I respond: 

- Irene: can you confirm whether the SOC2 control matrix we have maps fully to the SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet we bundle? FinRise may ask for a control-by-control crosswalk (they explicitly requested it). If we don't have a public crosswalk, can we generate one from the latest audit artifacts?
- Connor: product question — for the US-only deployment option, what are the expected log retention defaults and whether we can enable a 7-year log retention for enterprise customers without adding subprocessor approvals? Also need to confirm which subprocessors (cloud provider logging pipeline, analytics) have access to raw logs.

I want to offer FinRise the standard + enterprise retention language but call out any blockers so they know what to expect in the MAP. Also thinking we should include a short "acceptance checklist" that lists minimum items required for conditional acceptance (SOC2 letter + DPA signed + CAIQ Q&As + confirmation of retention tier).

If you can send bullet answers by EOD 3/22 I will update the MAP and send final to Aisha.

Thanks — Evelyn

From: Aisha Benton <aisha@finrise.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Liao <victor.liao@finrise.com>
Date: 2027-03-23T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — security gates + data retention needs

Evelyn — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. The MAP PDF covers most items; our legal has a couple of retention redlines on the DPA which we'll share tomorrow. Two follow-ups for clarity before our acceptance decision: 

1) Can you confirm the exact log export format (JSONL sample) and if scheduled exports are available for customer retention archives?
2) For the enterprise retention tier (up to 7 yrs), are backups encrypted with a customer-managed key (KMS) or Redwood-managed key, and what is the process for key-rotation audits?

If you can answer those two bullets (even briefly) and we get the DPA minor redlines addressed, we are optimistic about a conditional acceptance on 3/28. Could you also enable a short telecon Wednesday afternoon if needed for final clarifications?

Cheers,
Aisha
attachments: FinRise_DPA_redlines_20270323.docx
